diagnostics.message: Unterminated string; add a closing quote.
'{ch}' is not valid here.
'{name}' reads as a quantity ({value} {unit}), not a name. Try '{suggestion}'.
'{word}' is reserved. Choose another name.
Only the first '{section}' section is used.
Connections must come after the 'connections' line.
A {statement} cannot appear after the '{section}' line.
Cannot read this line. Expected a component declaration or a connection.
'{token}' looks like a parameter but has no value. Write '{token}=…'.
Put this under a 'schedule' line.
'{circuit}' is solved as a steady state, so its schedule does not run. Write 'fluid dynamic' to solve it in time.
'{text}' — a name cannot contain '-'. Write '{underscored}'.
'{word}' is not an attachment. Write 'inlet {node}' or 'outlet {node}'.
'{word}' needs one node of the parent circuit, and may appear once per circuit.
A 'control' line needs named arguments, such as 'control actuate=V1.position measure=N2.t by=PID1'.
'{word}' applies to the whole file and must come before the first 'circuit' line.
Spacing is in world units, so write 'spacing {n}' with no unit.
'{extra}' is more than this line can hold.
Put this pair under a 'curve' line.
'curve {name}' needs what it depends on, such as 'curve {name} tout'.
A curve row is one x and one y, such as '-26 50'.
A 'design' line needs named values, such as 'design tout=-26'.
Ignoring style '{token}'. Expected a colour, a width, a corner style, or a line pattern.
'{a}' overrides the earlier '{b}'.
'#' starts a comment; the rest of this line was ignored. Write the colour as "{hex}".
No style called '{name}' is defined; the components keep their previous style.
Style '{name}' is defined again; the later definition is used.
Cannot add two {dimension}s. To offset by a difference, write '{example}'.
'{parameter}' is a {expected}; '{value}' is a {actual}.
Cannot {operation} a {left} and a {right}.
{parameter} = {value} is outside the usual range ({low}–{high}). Check the unit.
{parameter} cannot be negative.
'{component}' is a {kind}, whose power is a capacity: {value} is read as {magnitude}. Write it positive, or use 'heat_exchanger' for a signed heat flow.
'{name}' is already defined at line {line}.
'{name}' depends on itself: {cycle}.
Dividing by zero here. '{expression}' is zero.
Nothing named '{name}'.
A {kind} has no '{property}'. It has: {available}.
No function '{name}'. Available: {available}.
'{function}' takes {expected} arguments.
'{name}' is already declared at line {line}. Names are unique across the whole file; tags are what distinguish circuits.
There is no '{kind}'.
A {kind} has no '{parameter}'. It accepts: {available}.
'{name}' is a value, not a component.
A {kind} has no port '{port}'. Ports: {available}.
Port '{port}' of '{name}' is already connected at line {line}.
'{name}' is not connected to anything.
No circuit name; using '{name}'.
Added {kind} '{name}' ({rule}).
'{name}' and {count} others are not connected to the rest of the circuit.
Read '{written}' as '{canonical}'.
'{written}' could be '{first}' or '{second}'. Write one of them.
'{parameter}' accepts {available}; '{written}' is none of them.
'{parameter}' names a component property, like 'N2.t'.
'{written}' is outside {kind}'s supported {min}…{max} range.
'{circuit}' is {circuitMode} while the project is {projectMode}; the circuit's own setting is used.
'{name}' is not declared anywhere. A subcircuit attaches to a node of another circuit.
'{name}' is not a known circuit role, so it is placed neutrally. Known roles: {available}.
'{circuit}' declares '{present} {node}' and no '{other}'. A subcircuit attaches with both.
A 'control' line needs {list}. Missing: {missing}.
'{param}' of '{component}' cannot be controlled.
'{name}' is a {kind}, not a controller.
Circuit {number} is already '{owner}'. Every circuit's number is its own.
'{name}' is already a circuit at line {line}.
'{circuit}' takes flow from '{a}' and returns it to '{b}'. A subcircuit attaches to one parent; write the second link as a connection.
'{driver}' is not something '{curve}' can depend on. Name a curve, a known driver, or 'time'.
'{curve}' depends on '{driver}', which has no value here. Add 'design {driver}=...' or solve in time.
'{curve}' has two rows at {x}; the later one is used.
'{curve}' needs at least two rows to interpolate between.
A {kind} has no single {role} to use here. Write it out, such as '{example}'.
'{name}' is a {kind}, which is not placed with 'at'. Connect it with '-' instead.
'{name}' observes nothing. Place it with 'at' and the name of a node.
This draft states no language version. Add 'fluidscript {major}' as its first line to save it.
This file is FluidScript {major}, which this version cannot read. It understands {supported}.
This file says it is FluidScript {first} and also {second}. Delete the line that is wrong.
There is no fluid called '{name}'. Available: {list}.
Cannot fix a state from {a} and {b}; they are not independent here.
{name} data covers {lo} to {hi}; this state is at {value}.
Could not evaluate {property} for {name} at {state}.
Relative humidity must be between 0 and 100 %.
'{name}': {parameters} cannot all be set. Any {count} of them fix the rest.
'{name}': using kv={kv}; dp is implied by it.
'{name}': position must be between 0 and 1.
'{name}' is a dead end. Set t, p or flow to make it a boundary.
'{name}': efficiency must be between 0 and 1.
'{name}': in, out, in2, out2 and power already fix the thermal size. Remove {param}, or let a temperature be solved.
'{name}': '{param}' has no second-side profile to rate. State in2/out2/dt2/flow2, connect both secondary ports, or remove it.
{name} cannot transfer {power} kW: with {t_hot} and {t_cold} in, the most any exchanger could move is {qmax} kW.
'{name}': Coupled mode requires both in2 and out2 connections; {port} is open.
'{name}': state either t for every layer, or all of t1…t{layers}; do not mix them.
'{name}': layers must be a whole number from 1 to 100.
'{name}': {parameter} is a normalized level and must be between 0 (bottom) and 1 (top).
'{name}': a {kind} must state {parameter}.
'{name}': a {kind} must state {count} of {parameters}.
'{name}': power={power} means side {side} {duty}, but {inlet}={in} and {outlet}={out} say the water {change}. Flip the sign, swap the temperatures, or use a role word such as load or heater.
Using '{node}' as the pressure datum. Pressures are relative to it.
'{component}' port '{port}' is not connected; treating it as closed.
'{circuit}' is closed and its heat does not balance: {power} with nowhere to go. Add a load, a source, or a boundary.
'{circuit}' has a {present} and no {missing}. Fluid must both enter and leave, or neither.
This circuit is over-specified by {n}. Remove one of: {list}.
This circuit is under-specified by {n}. Add one of: {list}.
'{a}' and '{b}' both set a pressure on the same closed loop, with no path between them for flow to take. Remove one, or connect them.
'{list}' are not connected to the rest of the circuit.
Nothing drives flow around {loop}; it will carry none. Is a pump on the wrong leg?
{substance} cannot be at {state}.
'{component}' touches {a} and {b} with no clear heat direction; tagging it into {chosen}.
'{circuit}' attaches to '{node}', which is one of its own components. A subcircuit attaches to another circuit.
'{constraint}' is held by '{pump}', which is not on its branch. Every pump on that branch is stated or already claimed; if one was meant to hold this flow, free it.
'{second}' at {b} m is wired directly to '{first}' at {a} m. Put a pipe between them, or give them one height.
'{node}' is {rise} m above '{datum}', which puts it {short} kPa below the lowest pressure {substance} can be at. State a pressure on '{datum}' of at least {needed} kPa.
The circuit closes on itself, so components are ordered by a depth-first walk from the pressure datum.
'{group}' has {count} members and will start collapsed; expand it on the canvas to see them.
'{circuit}' is named as a {role} circuit but its stated duties make it a {stage}; the duties decide where it is drawn.
'{component}.{field}' is {value} and cannot be written in {unit}; the field is sent empty.
The model is {size} KiB with states, over the {cap} KiB cap; states are omitted and can be fetched per component.
No catalogue '{name}'. Available: {list}.
Catalogue '{name}' is invalid: {reason}.
Catalogue '{name}' has {count} row(s) without two verified public sources, starting at '{first}'. An unverified dimension is a wrong design nobody can see.
Using catalogue '{name}'. Write 'catalog {name}' to pin it.
Could not solve in {steps} steps. Furthest off: {component} {equation} by {amount}.
The circuit has no unique solution around {component}. Check for a missing pressure datum, a closed circuit with no stated temperature, or a loop with no driver.
The solution is moving away from a balance: {residual} after {steps} steps, from {previous}.
Stuck at {residual}: {component} {equation} may have conflicting requirements.
{solver} cannot solve this: {reason}.
Solve cancelled after {steps} steps.
{component} produced an impossible value in {equation} after {steps} steps.
{parameter} was held at {bound}, which is as far as it goes. The circuit is asking for more than this component can give: check the duty, the resistance, or a stated temperature it cannot reach.
Nothing in the circuit determines {combination}. These move together and no equation separates them, so a value stated for any one of them determines the rest.

{combination} are not independent: one of them is already implied by the others, so the circuit constrains one thing fewer than it appears to. Stating something elsewhere will not help — one of these has to change.
Taking a reduced step near {component}; the solution is hard to reach here.
{component} carries {flow} kg/s from '{outlet}' to '{inlet}', against its written direction{note}.
'{name}': the approach is {approach} K, below the {minimum} K it must respect. Raise the duty's temperature difference, or accept a closer approach with approach={approach}.
The script has {count} {what}; the limit is {max}, so it is not solved.
The drawing breaks its own {rule} rule between '{first}' and '{second}' ({detail}); the picture is unreliable there.
